create.title: Subcritical angular-symbol collapse to a one-sided character-divisor cone
create.statement_tex: Put Y=sqrt(X), y=floor(sqrt(X)), and d_(n,h)=2h sqrt(X/n). The exact angular multiplier satisfies Omega_X^*(n,h)=1_(d_(n,h)<=y)^*+O(min(1,n/Y)); the floor-, activity-, bottom-, partition-, and star-safe proof is nontrivial on n<=9Y/4. On every fixed block n asymp N=X^nu with 0<nu<1/2, the hard coefficient is eventually exactly D(n)=sum_(hq=n,q odd,q>4h) chi_4(q)=sum_(q|n,q odd,q>2sqrt(n)) chi_4(q), with no equality star. For fixed smooth V the normalized radial replacement error is O_V(N^(5/4)log(2N)/Y), power-saving for nu<2/5 and X^epsilon-safe with a logarithm at nu=2/5. The remaining signed one-sided radial sum is open and has polynomial absolute capacity.
create.next_action: Attack the exact one-sided coefficient through its false-theta generating function sum_(h>=1) z^(4h^2+h)/(1+z^(2h)); seek a coefficient-preserving transformation or signed radial estimate and audit partial-theta/Appell literature before import.

update.next_action: For smooth lower-radial blocks through nu=2/5, the exact symbol replacement is target-safe. Prove the signed one-sided character-divisor radial estimate, preferably through the exact false-theta/Appell-type generating kernel; retain a separate signed correction above nu=2/5.
Use the proved subcritical collapse. Below the two-fifths replacement threshold, estimate the exact one-sided divisor cone; do not replace it by r_2/4 or discard its angular projector.

The angular symbol is reduced to the exact one-sided coefficient with target-safe error through nu=2/5. The signed cone remains open there, and both the signed correction and cone remain open above nu=2/5.

reject.reason: The telescope leaves the asymmetric cone q>4h. Its coefficient is an incomplete character-divisor prefix and is not r_2(n)/4.
The replacement error is target-safe through nu=2/5, but the limiting signed one-sided sum has polynomial absolute capacity and remains unproved.
At nu=2/5 the replacement error is O(log X), which is admissible under an X^epsilon target.
Popov's theorem uses the complete r_2 coefficient. The joint cutoff q>4h destroys that complete convolution and is not covered by the theorem.

no_change.reason: The signed one-sided lower-radial sum and the remaining subcritical range are open.
The promoted result is a reduction and proves no new discrepancy exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 62 eliminates the complete floor-perturbed angular profile on the lower radial range, identifies an exact X-independent one-sided arithmetic coefficient, and closes its replacement error through nu=2/5. It does not estimate the remaining signed cone or improve the final exponent.
